about: SORT (ADR-0125): an array ordered by one of its columns or rows; it spills.

cases.description: Descending: the largest first
Descending: the smallest last
By the first column, ascending, when nothing more is given
Equal keys keep their order
By the second column, descending
by_col sorts the columns by a row
An index past the array is #VALUE!
An order other than 1 and -1 is #VALUE!
Text sorts without regard to case
Numbers sort before text, and text before booleans
A blank key sorts after the 7, so the Anchor shows 7
A blank key's spilled cell, below the 7 of SORT-011, shows 0
In a descending sort a blank key is still last, so the 7 comes first
A blank key among text sorts last, neither as empty text nor as 0, either of which would come first

Over 7 and then #N/A the Anchor shows 7: an Error Value key is neither the result nor sorted before a number. The #N/A followed the 7 already, so this fits an Error Value key that sorts after the numbers and one that keeps its place alike (SORT-026 asks which)
In a descending sort of text a blank key is still last, so b comes first
In a descending sort of text the blank key's cell is the last and shows 0
A blank key sorts after a boolean too, so TRUE is second
After a number and a boolean the blank key is last and shows 0
by_col, a blank key in the row sorts its column last, which shows 0
COUNTA counts a blank kept in SORT's array, read inside the Formula: 2 over 7 and a blank
A blank kept in SORT's array, taken out by INDEX, is still blank: neither the 0 it spills as nor empty text
In a descending sort two blank keys keep their order, so x is second, after the 1's z
Over b, a blank and a, b is second, after the a of SORT-014
Over b, a blank and a, the blank key is last and its cell shows 0
An Error Value key sorts after the numbers: the Anchor is 7, and the #N/A does not keep its place first (Windows run 18a)

Engine's answer, Excel to be asked: the Error Value key's own cell, after the 7 of SORT-015, shows the Error Value, where an Error Value key that sorts after the numbers and one that keeps its place both put it
An Error Value key comes first in a descending sort, the order of the kinds reversed: the Anchor is #N/A, not the 7 (Windows run 18a)
An Error Value key sorts after text: the Anchor is a (Windows run 18a)
An Error Value key sorts after a boolean: the Anchor is TRUE (Windows run 18a)
An Error Value key sorts before a blank key, which sorts last: the Anchor is #N/A, not the 0 the blank spills as (Windows run 18a)

Two different Error Value keys do not keep their order: #DIV/0! sorts before #N/A, as ERROR.TYPE numbers them, 2 before 7, and as their texts sort, which this case does not tell apart (Windows run 18a)
Engine's answer, Excel to be asked: SUM adds nothing for a blank kept in SORT's array, whether it passes over it or reads it as 0, where the sum does not nearly cancel
COUNT does not count a blank kept in SORT's array, as it does not count a blank cell: 1, not 2 (Windows run 18a)
COUNTA counts the blank INDEX takes out of SORT's array as one Value, as it counts it in the array (SORT-021): 1, not 0 (Windows run 18a)
Engine's answer, Excel to be asked: a Formula whose result is the blank INDEX takes out of SORT's array shows 0, as one that reads a blank cell does
SUM passes over a blank kept last in SORT's array, so that its last addition, of 0.2, cancels: 0, not 2.78E-17 as with the blank added last as 0 (Windows run 18a)
SORT given the blank FILTER keeps as a key sorts it last, as a blank cell's key (SORT-011): the Anchor is 7, not 0 (Windows run 18a)
IF hands SORT's array on with its kept blank as it is, which ISBLANK reads blank, TRUE, as it read it out of SORT (SORT-022), not the 0 it spills as (Windows run 18a)

Engine's answer, Excel to be asked: in a descending sort a blank key sorts after a boolean too, as Excel's did after numbers and text (SORT-013, 016) and after a boolean ascending (SORT-018), so the last cell is the blank's and shows 0; not 0 if the blank sorted first

Engine's answer, Excel to be asked: in an ascending sort two blank keys keep their order, as Excel kept equal keys (SORT-004) and two blank keys in a descending sort (SORT-023), so x is second, after the 1's z; y if they were reversed
A sort_index that is not a whole number is truncated: 1.5 sorts by the first column and the Anchor is 1; rounded to 2 it would sort by the second and give 3 (Windows run 18a)
